text:
marta: quick sync — we need a smoke signoff for FlashAttention v2/v3 integration tonight. spotted a ~8-12% tail latency regression on long-seq fused attention in the perf run, and KV cache churn spikes during bursty chat loads. planning to gate with flags + narrow canary.

raj: can you paste the perf numbers? is it iso A/B vs current kernel chooser?

marta: yes, A/B vs current chooser. 99th went from 210ms -> 230-235ms on sequences > 1024 with fused path enabled under synthetic ramp. average token cost unchanged. KV churn correlates with bursty sessions that do a lot of prefix edits.

lee: sounds like an eviction/regeneration thrash. did profiler show increased memcpy / CUDA syncs?

marta: profiler shows extra device->host syncs in fallback path when fused kernel hits cornercase, and a spike in KV eviction calls. attaching quick snippet:

```
# simplified perf trace
t=0  dispatch -> fused_kernel_fast_path
t=14ms  fused_kernel -> fallback_path (memcpy)   # unexpected
t=18ms  kv_cache.evict(batch=12)
t=30ms  request complete
```

nina: for the gate we need exact canary percentages + telemetry. propose: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 6h windows with rollback if 95th or 99th regresses >5% or error rate increases >0.1%.

marta: agree. rollout checklist:
- feature flag `flashattn.v3_select` default off
- small canary (0.1%) pinned to non-critical tenants
- perf test harness running real chat traces during canary
- KV eviction metrics + KV miss ratio alerts
- automated rollback hook on regressions

lee: recommend adding a micro-canary that forces `paged-attn` fallback for a few sessions to confirm behavior, i.e., exercise fallback path deliberately.

infra-bot: canary job created: job_id=canary-394321-1, targets=0.1% traffic, baseline window=30m. telemetry: latency.hist, errors.count, kv.evictions, kv.misses. Link: https://ci.internal/canaries/canary-394321-1

ops: what about model routing? if we see capacity stress, do we fallback to older model variant or to non-fused kernel? which is safer?

marta: plan is kernel-first fallback (to v2 fused/non-fused selector) followed by routing to lower-capacity model variant if kernels overwhelmed. fallback priority: 1) kernel selector -> v2 compatibility, 2) paged-attn fallback, 3) reroute to smaller model.

devex-bot: checklist doc updated: https://confluence.internal/flashattn/integration-smoke-394321 (contains curl snippets and dashboards).

marta: operational commands (use with care):
```
# toggle feature flag for team 'canary-team'
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_API" \
  https://flags.internal/api/toggle \
  -d '{"flag":"flashattn.v3_select","team":"canary-team","state":"on"}'
```

raj: two quick asks before we go: 1) add a short-run load test using real user prefix edits to reproduce KV churn, 2) ensure canary tenants aren't heavy-embed users (embedding workloads distort token metrics).

marta: noted. I'll kick off the edit-heavy load test now and share results. target is to get first 0.1% canary in next 90m if tests look stable.

infra-bot: load test queued: lt-394321-edits (30m). will post results to the canary page.

nina: also add an alert that watches for sudden increase in device memory alloc/free counts — that correlated with the fallback pathology in last incident.

marta: good call. adding memory alloc alert with 3x baseline threshold.

ops: if anything unexpected, we abort and set flag off globally. no manual partial fixes unless eng-runtime leads approve. :thumbsup:

marta: thanks all — I'll post canary status updates here. next update after first 0.1% window (~90m).
